correctness.rationale: Convex group averaging over S_a×S_r reduces global SLEM minimization to p,q,s with hub budget ap+rq≤1. Full three-group quotient Laplacian has positive roots alpha_± of z²−[(a+1)p+(r+1)q]z+(a+r+1)pq, while leaf and core transverse eigenvalues are 1−q and 1−p−as. Increasing p at fixed q increases the positive quotient gap. At saturation, the exact G_(N/H)(q)=−Nr[q−(2a+1)/H]² forces alpha_-≤N/H. When r≤a, q=(2a+1)/H,p=(2r+1)/H,s=(1−p)/a attain SLEM (4ar−1)/H; for r≥a the leaf bottleneck q=1/(a+r), combined with G_u(q)<0 for q>u, forces SLEM 1−1/(a+r). Equality yields unique invariant hub-edge pair, not all non-invariant optimizers. Independent symbolic identities checked, direct full eigenspectra agreed in 100 pairs a,r=2..11. Finite tests do not prove all integers.
residual_risks: Proof covers symmetric uniform-stationary discrete-time stochastic kernels only; no global uniqueness outside invariant hub-edge probabilities.

value.rationale: The graph is a natural clique with single-hub pendant load, and its precise critical leaf count answers whether internal clique edges genuinely accelerate globally fastest uniform-stationary mixing. Exact all-size SLEM and invariant optimizer classification are mathematical spectral-design data that cannot be read from generic SDP formulations.

limitations: Special parameter r=a is included in both matching branches; a,r≥2 only.
